[b][u]OverView[/u][/b]
Hacknet is a puzzle game disguised as a nefarious hacking OS used to find flaws in systems around the globe. By using a Command-line Interface, the user will spend time trying to crack the into different computers and use the tools they are given to find solutions to seemingly impossible security systems. As the game progresses the user gains more tools, but tension builds as the user is faced with moral conundrums along with increasing tense situations as their quick wit and ability to type commands as fast as possible is put to the test.

[b][u]Gameplay[/u][/b]
Gameplay is rather simple, as stated before it functions much like a command-line interface. There are some [i]GUI[/i] elements you can use, but I [b]recommend[/b] you don't get too attached to them, cause in this world your computer is as vulnerable as the computers you hack into. Most of the interactions have you sign into or hack into servers, copy and destroy files, replace and decode systems, and a few other neat tech wizardry. You have programs as your main tool, however you are limited by RAM, so you must spend the time managing what programs you use and when. Every single program or tool you are given as well as commands will be used through all stages of the game.

[b][u]Story[/u][/b]
You've been sent this OS from an anonymous hacker who has tasked you with finding out what happened to him. He has Daemons (automatic tasks) setup to help you as you progress. He points you to hacker organizations as you get further and further into what Hacknet is, what it was built for and the ulterior motives of the Big Tech in charge.

[b][u]My take on it[/u][/b]
Fun game, has some tense moments but isn't too difficult to pick up even if you're not tech literate. Story's a bit short, but the game brings some neat moral questions and gives you multiple routes to the end. Oh and music is 👌

[h1] INTRO [/h1]
The best way to describe Hacknet for me is that it's an experience. You will like it if you're curious about what you see in the trailers and on YouTube. The comparison to real hacking that I've seen around the Interwebs is there in the similarities with the commands that you type into a terminal window, and the use of I.P. addresses, but that's really about it (Read about that here: https://www.quora.com/How-closely-is-HackNet-OS-game-related-to-the-real-life-hacking). But besides all of that, you should give it a go. It's $15, and it was worth every dime. I'll go into details below about why, but I would blanket recommend this game if you've seen anything interesting in the trailers, reviews, or content about this game. 

[h1] BEGINNING [/h1]
I'll go chronologically here: I found this game in a weird way. I found Furi through Dunkey's Best of 2017, and while listening to the Soundtrack for it Payload came on thanks to shuffle. I'll get to the soundtrack a "Bit" later, but Payload is one heck of an advertisement for Hacknet. The developer Matt Trobbiani said that the tutorial was what he was most proud of, which comes right when you start a New Session (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=suQ_dT8ucVg 0:52). I found that it was... lacking. I was unsure of how to solve most problems at the beginning of the game that I was presented with, and the convoluted explanations of what the commands did was not helpful for knowing what exactly to do with them. My examples here are the explanation of Shells and an Executable that I can't remember. If you're anything like me, the first hour(s) will be a grind: learning the commands, getting a feel for what the missions are asking of you, and learning the flow of the game. [i] Note: I found that saying what's wrong plainly will help with finding a solution. For example: "My file got deleted, I need another one. I'll just go and steal it". [/i] This was my challenge, and I found myself on the incredibly helpful Steam guide more than a few times in the early game (DO NOT USE THIS UNTIL YOU ARE STUCK https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=499723234). This was a more sufficient tutorial for getting accustomed to the game and progressing. But that's just the beginning of the game, and the game's biggest fault in my opinion. 

[h1] MID GAME [/h1]
After my mixed experience with the beginning of the game, things got better, and quickly. After you know the commands well and how they are used, (shell, rm, probe, connect, addnote, append/replace, upload, and a few more basics) you start to see the timing the game expects of you. The Trace adds real intensity to the game that will the expanded upon later. It really gets exciting as the commands come naturally to you. I disagree with Matt about the success of the tutorial, rather I would praise him on the pacing and creativity of the mid and the beautiful, beautiful, oh so beautiful endgame. I found myself going back to the guide less and less, and realizing that most problems can be solved with basic knowledge of the game, and a curiosity for combing through systems. You've got to look carefully through everything. You'll find everything from weird conversations to passwords that you can't proceed without. The flow of the mid game is quite enjoyable as the difficulty slowly picks up and your Net Map gets bigger and bigger. You start to get the sense that Hacknet is an open world game, which it is. Hacknet takes you through the mid game and cleverly prepares you for the final challenges that you will be ready for if you've paid attention throughout the game, and you won't have to use any guides at all. 

[h1] ENDGAME [/h1]
Hacknet's final challenge is daunting, but well-designed. Now for the ending. I won't say too much because it is best experienced without expectation, but I will say that it made it all worth it. Learning the commands, how the game is played, it all comes together. In a rather mild game, the experience of the ending is quite "shocking". This was where Hacknet was completely untouchable. I would give any amount of money to go back and experience that ending for the first time again. Best part of the game, by far. Sequencer is my favorite Executable and it will be yours as well once you finish the game. Now to the soundtrack, because this section and the next one go hand-in-hand. 

[h1] MUSIC [/h1]
Now I'm a music guy, and the soundtrack plays a huge role in Hacknet's overall experience. That's because there are almost no sound effects, the beeping of the Trace timer, accepting and competing contracts, and an Incoming Signal are all of the ones I can think of right now. If you turned the music off in settings, the game would be silent. Therefore there is a huge emphasis on the soundtrack. And I'll just say that I'm listening to Roja Drifts By just to get in the spirit for this section. There's a few really good ones, and the rest are ok. Here's a list of the good stuff: Carpenter Brut for obvious reasons, Tetrameth, Roja Drifts By, Outrun the Wolves, and in Labyrinths Dream Head, and even the legendary Resonance makes an appearance (at one point Matt said he thought he wouldn't make enough money to pay the artists back). The rest of the soundtrack was nice and "techno-y" and perfectly fit with the theme of the game and what you see on your screen. But the standout for me was obviously Remi Gallego. Everything he's put out, especially for Hacknet and Labyrinths turned out to be some of my favorite songs ever. Payload, Panic Track (which is basically Malware Injection), ClearText, and Sabotage were all masterpiece songs. I encourage you to check out the work he did on Hell is Other Demons as well if you liked his stuff here, it's great. However mentioning Payload gives me the opportunity to talk about the one problem that Hacknet has with its use of the soundtrack. I know Payload appears in Labyrinths, but the problem occurs in the main game as well. The songs are just set to repeat until you complete a contract or two (I also did not appreciate Matt cutting out the glitching in Payload, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4l6arwAIA6w 4:03). It gets old, and I found myself muting the music for a while to keep all of the tracks fresh because they are reused at points. 

[h1] STORY [/h1]
Lastly I'll touch on the story here, it's good. There's a Bit of a twist as to the fate of Hacknet which I thought was really cool, but it was also a bit convoluted. Took me some reading afterwards to figure out what just happened, but that's also because I wasn't really paying attention to the story and more worrying about why I couldn't complete some mission. Let's just say it's not spelled out, but I guess some players understood it pretty easily (THIS IS A STEAM FORUM ABOUT THE ENDING AND EXPLAINING IT, I AM ONLY INCLUDING IT TO SHOW THAT THE ENDING IS EXPLAINED IF YOU LOOK FOR IT https://steamcommunity.com/app/365450/discussions/0/530649887207612803/). Anyways, the story is strong and interesting, but you don't play it for the story. It's interesting enough that you could, but you just don't. 

[h1] SUMMARY & RATING [/h1]
Overall an unforgettable experience. Easter eggs, music, intensity, it's fun for the whole family (not really suitable for the whole family). Be patient in the beginning, learn the commands, comb through the systems, learn what is required of you. There are bumps and surprises waiting for you, and you're rewarded for jumping through each hurdle. Please give this a shot, I found music that I loved, an ending so good I pooped myself, I fought my way through an unfamiliar system, and I learned about video games. There's bound to be something you like about the game if you [b] stick with it [/b]. And if you liked what you played in the main game, get Labyrinths (https://store.steampowered.com/app/521840/Hacknet__Labyrinths/). You won't be sorry, mate. Matt put a lot of love into this game, and it shows. [b] 9/10. [/b]

Late review, but still... Hacknet is one of my favorite games and it was a really engaging experience. I often lost myself for hours in the game 'hacking' different servers/computers and I really recommend it to anyone who likes to puzzle a lot, while using unix. 

PRO's:
- Easy to learn, easy to master, but it doesn't make the game boring. On the contrary, it makes the game even more enjoyable, because (after mastering 'the controlls') you get the feeling of being a skilled 'hacker'.
- Probably the closest a game could get to real world hacking. Uplink was great too, but outdated and not as fun as Hacknet. Also great that you can use the 'GUI' to select hosts or use the command line to connect and perform functions.
- Great Soundtrack, really fits the 'hacking' experience and makes your heart beat a little bit faster during the most intense scenes. I downloaded the soundtrack after beating the game, because of the thrill you get from it.
- Great DLC (Hacknet Labrynths). I really liked the way that the Devs enabled players to make their own storylines, factions, puzzles, eastereggs, etc. while keeping the Hacknet game mechanics. I tried to make my own 'Extension', but after all it was harder than I thought. 
- Fun easter eggs. Took some time to get the last achievements, but it was totally worth it.

CON's:
- Storyline is too short and can be completed in a short time period. I almost felt sad when I completed the game (as there was DLC at the time, which meant that there was no new content to play).
- There are no consequnces to your actions. This means that you won't be attacked by enemies (in game of course) if you hack the wrong pc/server. Of course, there are some moments when a countdown is presented and you need to finish a task in a small amount of time, but besides that it gives you the feeling that nobody cares if they are hacked. Also, why should you ever clear logs and footprints when nobody will ever try to get you back using them?

Overall, definitely worth the money and it's a great game to get the 'hacking' vibe. Implementation of Extensions by the Devs makes the amount of content for this game even bigger, which means more storylines and time spent hacking with a cheeto dust covered keyboard.

Thanks for this wonderful experience.

The Good:
-Incredibly nostalgic for people who came up in the day of IRC chat and cracking local WEP keys for fun,
-The style and gameplay feel spot on for what its trying to convey
-Engaging and fair puzzles that make you think beyond sheer mechanics.
-Priced fairly
-The visuals commonplace to Hollywood Hacking are really well done and help draw the layman in. 

The Bad
-Relatively short
-Excess mechanics. Never once used trapping and many other features were never needed.
-Some missions ask more of you than than the engine is capable of doing, and you spend extra time trying to accomplish something the game doesn't even check for. 
-Repetitive. There is little variation between the nodes you try to crack, and each hacking tool only has about 3 different port addresses to break into. The little details of the story quickly fade into obscurity as the player figures out how to  scan the nodes for the trigger to advance. 
-Uninspired story. Without giving any spoilers, I'll just say that there is nothing to make the story feel tangible. At one point the game brings the player to a moment that feels like it should be a moral battle, but its so late in the game that you won't even be thinking about that, and just tying to plow ahead to the end. 
-Zero Replayability. This is a story based game. Once its played out out, there is no incentive to go back. There are parts that seem like they would have alternate pathways, but its just the player imagining the game to be something more than it is.  

Overall - Even with the expansion,  Hacknet is still cheaper than  going to the movies, and can be broken up over two days of casual play. Its feels very familiar to the old school text based adventures, with a little more arcade like mechanics as the driving force. You won't be blown away, but it is a fine one-off distraction. An arcade-puzzle game that will take most people a little over 10 hours.

[h1]Hacking simulator[/h1]

HACKNET is a game where our goal is to hack computers. This is related to a story that is not the most important here. The most important is the ability to hack other computers. We can hack ports, try to get access to mobile devices. It's not always as simple as in the first missions and indeed the further in the story the harder it is to hack some computers. Sometimes if we do a good search, we can get a password to some computer and that will bypass the hacking process.

Unfortunately, hacking is only interesting at first. Later it is a tedious repetition of the same moves. And that's when we start focusing more on the interesting story. 

The layout is satisfactory. We have the main screen where we have the necessary information. On the right side there is a terminal, where we enter commands, and on the right side open programs pop up. Below we have a map of connections, which was not very clear for me and some computers overlapped with others.

[h1]Summary[/h1]

I think it's worth playing this game if you're at least a little interested in the subject of hacking. For others, I strongly advise against it. The game can be boring for you and not worth buying. Nevertheless, I think it is a good game and I will be happy to return to it one day.

Grabbed this as part of the Australia wildfire bundle (it was actually the main reason I sprung for it), and I honestly really enjoyed it.  The base gameplay loop is surprisingly satisfying for what it is, being an even mix of high-paced process management and slower crawls through secure networks trying to find any little gap in security there is.  Sort of an off-puzzle game.  I only really have two gripes; the first is that the difficulty curve just sort of doesn't exist.  There aren't many notably complex networks, and the ones that DO exist are at the end of their campaign tracks.  It sort of makes it feel as though things end right as they're starting to get good.  The second is that if you get the bad ending on the DLC, you can't try again on that file.  I totally panicked on my go of it and only barely didn't manage to get to rebuilding the firmware in time.  Apart from that, though, very fun game.
